claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing a controlled density of nanoscale precipitates within the lamellar colonies can overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
Introducing nanoscale precipitates can retain or increase strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Nanoscale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
Obstruction of dislocation movement by nanoscale precipitates reduces dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups lowers local stress concentrations near internal boundaries.
Lower local stress concentrations reduce microcracking and catastrophic damage during straining.
The precipitate-mediated mechanism improves tensile ductility without compromising strength.
The predicted benefit applies at room temperature under conventional tensile-testing conditions.
The optimal precipitate density, size, and distribution for maximizing ductility and strength are unknown.
